recipes.name: Party Pizzas
ingredients_raw: 1 pound fresh, ground spicy pork sausage

steps.text: Preheat oven to 375 degrees F (190 degrees C).
Brown the ground beef and sausage together in a large skillet and drain well.

Cut the processed cheese into small cubes and add to the meat mixture. Cook over low heat, stirring frequently, until the cheese melts. Stir in hot pepper sauce to taste. Spread a layer of the meat and cheese mixture on slices of party rye bread. Arrange the slices on an ungreased cookie sheet.
Bake at 375 degrees F (190 degrees C) for 15 to 20 minutes, or until browned. Serve warm.

raw_recipe.headline: Party Pizzas
raw_recipe.description: These little pizzas are super easy and make the perfect appetizer. They are little pizzas, made with sausage, cheese and a bit of hot pepper sauce on cocktail bread. Men especially seem to like its hearty flavor.

review.reviewBody: These are delicious!!! My family has made these for YEARS and there are NEVER any left over. They are the perfect appetizer to take anywhere. Highly recommended!

1.21.17 I like the combination of the ground beef and spicy pork sausage (I used Jimmy Dean Hot), but I think this could be improved by adding something to this base. I could see a little spaghetti sauce, pizza sauce, tomato sauce, even salsa, just something to give this a little moisture...it's already cooked, but you still have to bake them. I used a pretty good shot of Sriracha, but could even see adding some red pepper flakes if you want to kick it up even more!. I think you could substitute some other cheeses for the American cheese, I’ll try shredded cheddar next time. Also, watch your time in the oven. Although the recipe says 15-20 minutes, mine were overcooked and a bit dry at 8 minutes; next time I’ll probably pull them out of the oven at 5 minutes. From an eye appeal perspective, I thought they needed something, so I added some chopped tomato which gave them a little pop of color, but you can use your imagination of how to garnish, maybe some shredded cheese or chopped jalapeño, whatever...sky’s the limit there.
My aunt brought something similar to this to our family christmas dinner. I really enjoyed them.
